full_judgment: 12. Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division perusing the Lower Court's Records and consequently upon non-consideration of the material evidence particularly the operative portion of the document under pre-emption showing the case land appertaining to holding of S.A. Khatian No.57/1 the home of Ramesh Chandra Bhattacharja on the basis of mutation in which the pre-emptor was not a co-sharer wrongly found that the pre-emptee petitioners could not prove that Jama of case Khatians were separated and separate Khatians were prepared so as to disown the claims of the pre-emptor as co-sharer of the lands of the case Khatian and the High Court Division failed to advert to the grounds taken in Revisional application that the Courts below committed error in the decision occasioning failure of justice failing to appreciate that because of the repeal of the Bengal Tenancy Act with the publication of S.A. Khatian under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, prayer for Preemption under section 96 of the later Act as made on the basis of C.S. Khatian published under Bengal Tenancy Act no longer in force as not maintainable inasmuch as the provision and purport of section 96 of the Act could not be given retrospective application to the instant sale long after repeal of the Bengal Tenancy Act. He further submits that the High Court Division upon non-consideration of iota of material evidence failed to appreciate that, the principle of waiver, estoppel and acquiescence would operate from the date of contract of sale on 02.10.1963 taking place in presence of and through active negotiation of the pre-emptor and his maternal uncle opposite party Nos.6 and 7 wrongly concurred with the finding of the Appellate Court that the pre-emption case was not barred by the principle of waiver, estoppels and acquiescence and to appreciate that the pre-emption case was bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as categorically pointed out in the grounds of revisional application. He next submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate on consideration of evidence of collusive and fraudulent nature and character of the pre-emption case brought by his maternal uncles, opposite party Nos.6 and 7 of the pre-emption case failing to succeed on contest as sub-sequent transferees of the case land in the suit for specific performance of contract of sale litigating up to High Court Division. He finally submits that the pre-emption case was not maintainable by deposit of consideration of Tk.6,000/- on the basis of agreement dated 02.10.1963 when evidence of P.W.1, the pre-emptor and other evidence show the value of the case land on the date of the deed executed through Court was at least taka on Lac and, as such, impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed.
